title: Count Ways to Distribute Candies
summary: Determine the number of distinct ways to distribute n unique candies into k bags such that each bag contains at least one candy.
statement: Determine the number of distinct ways to distribute n unique candies into k bags such that each bag contains at least one candy. Two distributions are considered different if the candies in any bag are not identical in both distributions. The result should be given modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: There are n uniquely labeled candies and k unlabeled nonempty bags, with 1 <= k <= n <= 1000.
Bag order and candy order within a bag do not matter; only the partition into groups matters.
Return the number of distributions modulo 1000000007.
hints: Add labeled candies one at a time to an unlabeled set partition.
The new candy either starts a new bag or joins one of the existing bags.
S(n,k)=S(n-1,k-1)+k*S(n-1,k); build a fresh row for each candy.
The two cases are disjoint and exhaustive, and a fresh row retains the previous candy count for both terms.
editorial: The two cases are disjoint and exhaustive, and a fresh row retains the previous candy count for both terms.

tests.explanation: Choose which one candy stands alone; the other two share the second bag, giving three partitions.
The seven partitions consist of four one-plus-three splits and three two-plus-two splits.
